name: Refugee Status (Refugees Act 2021)

requirements.blocker_text: Application for refugee status must be made to the Commissioner, directly or through an authorized officer. A temporary pass valid 90 days is issued pending a decision, which the Commissioner must make within 90 days (extendable for reasonable cause). Rejected applicants may appeal to the Refugee Status Appeals Committee within 30 days, then to the High Court.
requirements.fix_path: Submit an application to the Commissioner for Refugee Affairs.

evidence_required.document: In-person interview testimony (legal representation optional, at own expense)

outcome.duration_length: indefinite, subject to durable-solution outcomes (repatriation, local integration, or resettlement)
outcome.physical_presence_requirement: generally required to reside within a Commissioner-designated area/county unless individually exempted

sources.title: Kenya Law (official government legal database) -- Refugees Act, 2021: refugee status determination process (application to the Commissioner, 90-day temporary pass, 90-day decision timeline extendable for cause, Refugee Status Appeals Committee then High Court appeal route, non-penalization for unlawful entry while an application is pending); recognized refugees may engage in gainful employment, enterprise, or a recognized profession/trade; must generally reside in Commissioner-designated areas/counties unless exempted, with movement passes available for travel outside designated areas; identity documents issued with status comparable to Foreign National Registration Certificates

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Kenya). Published on tier-1 sourcing directly from Kenya Law -- a notably strong sourcing position for a humanitarian route in this dataset, where asylum/refugee law has more often landed as tier-2 (NGO/UNHCR-hosted) or been entirely absent (Bangladesh, Pakistan, India all lack a codified domestic asylum law; Sudan and Somalia's equivalents were tier-2-only). STRUCTURAL FEATURE WORTH CONTRASTING DIRECTLY AGAINST BOTH EARLIER MODELS IN THIS DATASET: like Sudan, Kenya's law requires refugees to reside in designated areas (in Kenya's case, specific counties, historically including Dadaab and Kakuma) rather than allowing Uganda's fully open-border settlement model -- but unlike Sudan's blanket permission-required regime, Kenya's 2021 Act builds in an explicit exemption mechanism (the Commissioner may exempt individuals from the area-residence requirement) and a formal movement-pass system for travel outside designated areas, making it a genuinely intermediate model between Uganda's openness and Sudan's stricter encampment approach. Kenya hosts one of the world's largest and longest-standing refugee populations (predominantly Somali, given Somalia's decades of conflict -- see so_international_protection.json's mirror-image finding that Somalia is itself the source), concentrated in Dadaab and Kakuma camps, alongside a growing urban refugee population the 2021 Act was specifically designed to better accommodate (per NGO commentary retrieved in this build, though not modeled as a hard requirement here). work_rights set to 'restricted' rather than 'full' since the right is explicitly conditioned on holding qualifications 'recognized by competent authorities in Kenya', a real qualifying condition rather than an open right.
